name: Webhook
category_description: Core node - built-in logic, data or generic API functionality
description: Use the Webhook node to create webhooks, which can receive data from apps and services when an event occurs. It's a trigger node, which means it can start an n8n workflow. This allows services to connect to n8n and run a workflow

parameters.name: Webhook URLs
parameters.description: The Webhook node has two Webhook URLs: test and production. n8n displays the URLs at the top of the node panel

parameters.name: HTTP Method
parameters.description: The Webhook node supports standard HTTP Request Methods:

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: By default, this field contains a randomly generated webhook URL path, to avoid conflicts with other webhook nodes

parameters.name: Supported authentication methods
parameters.description: You can require authentication for any service calling your webhook URL. Choose from these authentication methods:

parameters.name: Using n8n User Auth (OAuth2)
parameters.description: Only users logged in to this n8n instance can call the webhook. The caller must send an OAuth2 bearer token issued by this instance. n8n resolves the token to the calling user and runs the execution as that user. End-user credentials resolve to the calling user's connected accounts under this mode
options: Any other request receives a 401 response. Only GET requests can be redirected

parameters.name: Calling a webhook that uses n8n User Auth (OAuth2)
parameters.description: n8n is the OAuth2 authorization server for the webhook. How the caller gets a bearer token depends on the caller:

parameters.name: Response Code
parameters.description: Customize the HTTP response code that the Webhook node returns upon successful execution. Select from common response codes or create a custom code

parameters.name: Response Data
parameters.description: Choose what data to include in the response body:
options: All Entries: The Webhook returns all the entries of the last node in an array
No Response Body: The Webhook returns without a body

parameters.name: Allowed Origins (CORS)
parameters.description: Set the permitted cross-origin domains. Enter a comma-separated list of URLs allowed for cross-origin non-preflight requests. Use * (default) to allow all origins

parameters.name: Binary Property
parameters.description: Enabling this setting allows the Webhook node to receive binary data, such as an image or audio file. Enter the name of the binary property to write the data of the received file to

parameters.name: Ignore Bots
parameters.description: Ignore requests from bots like link previewers and web crawlers

parameters.name: IP(s) Allowlist
parameters.description: Enable this to limit who (or what) can invoke a Webhook trigger URL. Enter a comma-separated list of allowed IP addresses. Access from IP addresses outside the allowlist throws a 403 error. If left blank, all IP addresses can invoke the webhook trigger URL

parameters.name: No Response Body
parameters.description: Enable this to prevent n8n sending a body with the response

parameters.name: OAuth2 Client
parameters.description: How n8n handles a request without a bearer token when Authentication is n8n User Auth (OAuth2). Auto-Detect (default) redirects browser navigations through the n8n sign-in page and requires a bearer token from everything else. Bearer Token Only always requires a bearer token and never redirects. Bro

parameters.name: Only Run If
parameters.description: An expression evaluated against the incoming request. The workflow only runs if the expression returns true. Use $json to access the request as { body, headers, params, query }. For example, {{ $json.body.campaign_id === 'user-research-invite' }}. Requests that don't match receive a 200 response wit

parameters.name: Raw Body
parameters.description: Specify that the Webhook node will receive data in a raw format, such as JSON or XML

parameters.name: Response Content-Type
parameters.description: Choose the format for the webhook body

parameters.name: Response Headers
parameters.description: Send extra headers in the Webhook response. Refer to MDN Web Docs | Response header to learn more about response headers

parameters.name: Property Name
parameters.description: by default, n8n returns all available data. You can choose to return a specific JSON key, so that n8n returns the value

common_issues.title: Listen for multiple HTTP methods
common_issues.summary: By default, the Webhook node accepts calls that use a single method. For example, it can accept GET or POST requests, but not both. If you want to accept calls using multiple methods:

common_issues.title: Use the HTTP Request node to trigger the Webhook node
common_issues.summary: The HTTP Request node makes HTTP requests to the URL you specify

common_issues.title: Use curl to trigger the Webhook node
common_issues.summary: You can use curl to make HTTP requests that trigger the Webhook node

common_issues.title: Send a response of type string
common_issues.summary: By default, the response format is JSON or an array. To send a response of type string:

common_issues.title: Test URL versus Production URL
common_issues.summary: n8n generates two Webhook URLs for each Webhook node: a Test URL and a Production URL

common_issues.title: IP addresses in whitelist are failing to connect
common_issues.summary: If you're unable to connect from IP addresses in your IP whitelist, check if you are running n8n behind a reverse proxy

common_issues.title: Only one webhook per path and method
common_issues.summary: n8n only permits registering one webhook for each path and HTTP method combination (for example, a GET request for /my-request). This avoids ambiguity over which webhook should receive requests

common_issues.title: Timeouts on n8n Cloud
common_issues.summary: n8n Cloud uses Cloudflare to protect against malicious traffic. If your webhook doesn't respond within 100 seconds, the incoming request will fail with a 524 status code
